boundary: Pyroclastic density currents of the 3-5 Aug 2026 paroxysm (~50 h from 08:30 on 3 Aug) stayed in the floors of Fuego's radial barrancas, running 5-7 km from the crater. Barranca Seca on the west flank was hit first and hardest (9+ pulses by 3 Aug afternoon), and flows later also ran down Taniluyá, Ceniza, Las Lajas and Honda, possibly Trinidad and El Jute (INSIVUMEH; IFRC 5 Aug). The edge to look for in NISAR is the narrow strip of decorrelated barranca floor against coherent interfluves. The communities on those interfluves (Panimaché I/II, Morelia, El Porvenir in Yepocapa) got ash and were evacuated, but the IFRC reported no damage to people or homes. Barranca Seca itself, where INSIVUMEH measured deposits at up to 195.6 °C (Prensa Libre, 26 Aug), is not mapped by name in OSM, so it has no item.

items.title: Pyroclastic flows down the Taniluyá barranca, beside Panimaché and Morelia
items.place: Río/Barranca Taniluyá where it passes Morelia, Yepocapa (OSM waterway, ~6 km SW of the crater)
items.what_it_shows: INSIVUMEH update (4 Aug 2026; special bulletin BEFGO_062_2026): pyroclastic density currents were 'recurrent in the Seca, Taniluyá, Ceniza, Las Lajas and Honda barrancas', travelling 5-7 km, and are the main threat to communities next to the SW-flank barrancas (Seca, Taniluyá, Ceniza). INSIVUMEH also warned of lahars in the same channels with that day's rain.
items.licence: Guatemalan government agency report; text cited, no image used
items.notes: Point is a vertex of OSM way 327127250 (Río Taniluya), ~6.3 km from the crater, within the stated 5-7 km run-out. The source does not say flows reached this exact point. SW-flank observation was partly blocked by cloud and ash (INSIVUMEH). Other OSM Taniluya segments: 14.41180, -90.94440 and 14.39584, -90.96146 (further downstream, probably beyond the run-out).

items.title: Panimaché I and II: ash on the roofs, families evacuated, homes standing
items.place: Panimaché (OSM hamlet), aldea Morelia area, San Pedro Yepocapa, Chimaltenango
items.what_it_shows: La Hora (4 Aug 2026): rescue patrols (ASONBOMD, with the army) evacuated families from Panimaché I and II and Morelia to the municipal hall in Santa Lucía Cotzumalguapa as a preventive measure. Ash covered roofs, crops and plantations in Morelia, Santa Sofía, Panimaché I and II, El Porvenir and Los Yucales. The IFRC field report of 5 Aug says no damage to people or homes was recorded. This is the spared side of the boundary: on the ridge ~1.6 km from the Taniluyá channel point (fuego-01).
items.notes: OSM has one 'Panimache' hamlet node; the I/II split is not mapped. The La Hora lead photo (ASONBOMD) shows families being helped to the Santa Lucía Cotzumalguapa shelter, not Panimaché itself, so it is not used. IFRC 5 Aug: https://reliefweb.int/report/guatemala/gtm-erupcion-volcanica-08-2026-actividad-volcan-fuego-guatemala-2026-08-05.

items.title: Morelia: ashfall and evacuation, no flow damage
items.place: Morelia (OSM village), San Pedro Yepocapa, Chimaltenango
items.what_it_shows: Named with Panimaché in the La Hora evacuation report (4 Aug 2026): families were moved out by rescue patrols, and ash coated roofs and crops. The Guatemalan Red Cross/IFRC sitrep (4 Aug) names communities 7-10 km from the crater in Yepocapa as the most exposed to Barranca Seca flows. Afterwards, IFRC (5 Aug) recorded no damage to people or homes.
items.notes: Point is the OSM Morelia village node (~10 km SW of the crater). Red Cross sitrep: https://reliefweb.int/report/guatemala/gtm-erupcion-volcanica-08-2026-actividad-volcan-fuego-guatemala-2026-08-04.

items.title: El Porvenir: preventive evacuation on the west flank
items.place: El Porvenir (OSM hamlet, Los Yucales), San Pedro Yepocapa
items.what_it_shows: The Watchers (4 Aug 2026) reports that SE-CONRED declared an institutional orange alert and ordered preventive evacuations in El Porvenir, Las Lajitas and nearby communities. La Hora lists El Porvenir and Los Yucales among the places where ash covered roofs and crops. No flow impact is reported here.
items.notes: The Watchers day page summarises a longer article ('Strong eruption at Fuego volcano produces pyroclastic...'). Las Lajitas is not in OSM, so it has no item. Point is the OSM El Porvenir hamlet node (~11 km WSW of the crater).

items.title: Barranca Las Lajas: flows down the southeast flank
items.place: Barranca Las Lajas, upper reach, Alotenango, Sacatepéquez (OSM waterway)
items.what_it_shows: INSIVUMEH (4 Aug) and the IFRC field report (5 Aug 2026) list Las Lajas among the barrancas with recurrent pyroclastic density currents, on the SE flank that INSIVUMEH could see clearly. This is the channel that buried San Miguel Los Lotes in 2018. In 2026 the IFRC reported no damage to homes.
items.credit: IFRC GO field report / Cruz Roja Guatemalteca, via ReliefWeb
items.licence: ReliefWeb/IFRC report; text cited, no image used
items.notes: Point is a vertex of OSM way 492664428 (Barranca Las Lajas), ~1.7 km SE of the crater, upstream of any settlement. Run-out length in this barranca is not given separately. Puente Las Lajas on the Ciudad Vieja-Escuintla road (14.41860, -90.82571) is in the window, but no 2026 report about it was found, so it is not included.
